SCHD is by far the best spot for beginners (share price and immediately higher returns) and retirees with the annual rebalancing taking the stress and management out of retirement years. If you retire with  have say 1k per month (3k per quarter)  in Roth income from SCHD shares (about 360k in todays dollars) and drew 750 per month and reinvested the other 250 (25% DRIP) you would have a supplemental tax free income that would increase faster than the pace of inflation and grow your income every year. Investors that are young (and thus their time horizon is long term) should invest in growth and concentrate on total return (capital appreciation plus dividends). I see too many youtubers and people that are young emphasizing dividend (and dividend growth) stocks. Their justification is to build a portfolio of income/dividend producing stocks or ETFs. However, if they are simply reinvesting that income/dividends, it would be more advantageous to get a better overall total return. Then later on in life transform their portfolio to stocks that produce income/dividends. Too much emphasis on high yield dividend stocks/ETFs at a young age will ultimately result in less overall wealth in the future. IMHO, it is better to select higher growth stocks that pay smaller yield dividends that are growing annually at a higher rate. Here is the reason why: What most people do not take into account is the importance of dividend growth. You must remember that a stock with a small dividend may still be paying a small dividend percentage-wise as time goes by even if it is increasing its dividend significantly, as long as the stock is appreciating at a high rate. So, even if a stock has a small dividend percentage-wise, but is growing both the dividend and capital appreciation, over time, the dividend paid will be higher and the capital appreciation will be greater than a stock that has a higher initial dividend with a slower dividend growth rate and slower capital appreciation over time. This has a similar impact as compounding interest. It is compounding dividend growth. Think about this carefully. This is a very important fact, especially for long term investors. SCHD is NOT a bad choice for a dividend ETF, since its dividend growth CAGR is pretty good. However, its capital appreciation is mediocre over the long term. The S&P 500 index ETF's (VOO, IVV, SPY) capital appreciation are better/higher and, therefore, their total returns over the past 10 years resulted in more overall wealth.  This YT video is evidence of this when it shows a comparison of SPY/SCHD/NOBL with a starting investment of $10k. SPY beat SCHD by 1.6% in the comparison.  That 1.6% over that comparison resulted in a total return of SPY beating SCHD by almost $10k. Although I do hold some SCHD, I mainly hold VOO and QQQ/QQQM (VOO slightly outperforms SPY due to the smaller expense ratio).  However, I favor holding individual dividend growth stocks. It does take time, effort and research to find stocks that will beat the ETFs consistently in both capital appreciation and dividend growth. Most people won't put in this time and effort, and there is nothing wrong with taking that route. It definitely is easier to just pick an ETF like SCHD (and maybe a few other ETFs). However, selectively picking individual stocks has been very rewarding financially (and mentally!!!). But that is just me because I enjoy doing so. Of course, what I am doing will probably be viewed as taking on more risk, and it may have more downside in a down market.  However, it has considerably more upside in the long term. Is it worth it? I guess that depends on the person.
